chapter: England, later career and closing thoughts
title: Staying home, real estate and the hope for a market
summary: She now rarely travels, owns a six-unit apartment house, serves on the union board, and believes recognition once earned is not lost.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: So you are still performing, for the record, here. I know you are. But you work clubs here in Los Angeles. You don't travel much, though, do you?

I don't travel too much now, no, I don't. I sort of stay home. Well, I'm an old landlady. I love dealing in real estate, so I inveted money in real estate. That is in an apartment house. And a six-unit place. I rent five ofthem and I live in one, and that sort of keeps me busy, that and my little, you know, chore with the board,the union, because sometimes we meet two or three times -- well, we meet once every week, and sometimes it's possible we meet maybe twice a week. So I'm quite busy with that. But I still love what I do. I love my work, and I feel that the time has come or will come when, you know, when you won't have to butt your head

against a stone wall, trying to really get into the scene as it is today. Because it's a whole different ball game, and at that time -- there are still people, there is still a market for whatever anybody has to offer, you know. Once you've made it. This is the way I feel. I feel once you've made it or got the recognition, you don't lose the recognition. But there are people who are looking for the next what else is new, so what else is new. And this is the thing that's a little heartbreaking about the whole thing, because the people -- there are people around today that could do and promote and could -- the same thing that did happen can happen again, it can happen. Because you don't lose this unless you lose your voice or lose your fingers or a hand, or lose, you know, lose your cool, as the kids say. You lose your cool, then that's it, you know.
